title: The 10,000-Hour Rule
coreMove: The 10,000-hour rule teaches that mastery requires deep practice, but deep practice depends on access to tools, feedback, time, and timing.

exampleSpecs.stakes: working students may never build enough practice hours
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Bill Joy at Michigan to allocate scarce coding lab access.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a band may miss the hard stage hours that build skill
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Translate the Beatles in Hamburg into a rehearsal design.

exampleSpecs.stakes: students without rare tools may never find their skill early
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Bill Gates and Lakeside to choose access over awards.

exampleSpecs.audience: coaches managing limited boards and mentors
exampleSpecs.stakes: new players may be kept from the feedback that grows mastery
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply practice opportunity to mentor time in chess.

exampleSpecs.stakes: new cooks may get praise without enough hard repetitions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the volume lesson to redesign kitchen practice.

exampleSpecs.stakes: confident users may crowd out first-time builders
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use practice opportunity to widen maker-space access.
